citation.authors: Liao W, Chen C, Wen T, Zhao Q

record.population: Adults taking antibiotics in 36 randomised, placebo-controlled trials
record.design: Meta-analysis of probiotics for preventing antibiotic-associated diarrhoea
record.finding: Probiotics reduced antibiotic-associated diarrhoea by 38 per cent (relative risk 0.62, 95% CI 0.51 to 0.74), more when started early. Adverse events were no more common than with placebo (relative risk 1.00).
record.note: Ethnicity not reported in the abstract. One use (antibiotic diarrhoea), which is not the same as everyday gut health.
